    "text": "If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to\na Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so\nthat it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match\nits topic name.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-6]\n\nWhen a new subscription is established, the last retained message, if\nany, on each matching topic name MUST be sent to the subscriber.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-7]\n\nIf the Server receives a QoS 0 message with the RETAIN flag set to 1 it\nMUST discard any message previously retained for that topic. It SHOULD\nstore the new QoS 0 message as the new retained message for that topic,\nbut MAY choose to discard it at any time - if this happens there will be\nno retained message for that topic.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-8]\n\nWhen sending a PUBLISH Packet to a Client the Server MUST set the RETAIN\nflag to 1 if a message is sent as a result of a new subscription being\nmade by a Client.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-9]\n\nIt MUST set the RETAIN flag to 0 when a PUBLISH Packet is sent to a\nClient because it matches an established subscription regardless of how\nthe flag was set in the message it received.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-10]\n\nA PUBLISH Packet with a RETAIN flag set to 1 and a payload containing\nzero bytes will be processed as normal by the Server and sent to Clients\nwith a subscription matching the topic name. Additionally any existing\nretained message with the same topic name MUST be removed and any future\nsubscribers for the topic will not receive a retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-11]\n\nA zero byte retained message MUST NOT be stored as a retained message on\nthe Server.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-12]\n\nIf the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a\nServer, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or\nreplace any existing retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.2-1]"
  },

Additionally any existing\nretained message with the same topic name MUST be removed and any future\nsubscribers for the topic will not receive a retained message\n[MQTT-3.3.1-10] . “As normal” means that the RETAIN flag is not set in\nthe message received by existing Clients. A zero byte retained message\nMUST NOT be stored as a retained message on the Server [MQTT-3.3.1-11] .\n\nIf the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a\nServer, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or\nreplace any existing retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-12] .\n\nNon normative comment\n\nRetained messages are useful where publishers send state messages on an\nirregular basis. A new subscriber will receive the most recent state.\n\nRemaining Length field\n\nThis is the length of variable header plus the length of the payload.\n\n3.3.2 Variable header\n\nThe variable header contains the following fields in the order: Topic\nName, Packet Identifier.\n\n3.3.2.1 Topic Name\n\nThe Topic Name identifies the information channel to which payload data\nis published.\n\nThe Topic Name MUST be present as the first field in the PUBLISH Packet\nVariable header. It MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string [MQTT-3.3.2-1] as\ndefined in section 1.5.3.\n\nThe Topic Name in the PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT contain wildcard\ncharacters [MQTT-3.3.2-2] ."
  },

    "text": "The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT Control\nPacket is set to zero and disconnect the Client if it is not zero.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-4]\n\nIf CleanSession is set to 0, the Server MUST resume communications with\nthe Client based on state from the current Session (as identified by the\nClient identifier). If there is no Session associated with the Client\nidentifier the Server MUST create a new Session. The Client and Server\nMUST store the Session after the Client and Server are disconnected.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-5]\n\nAfter the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the\nServer MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any\nsubscriptions that the client had at the time of disconnection as part\nof the Session state.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-6]\n\nIf CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any\nprevious Session and start a new one. This Session lasts as long as the\nNetwork Connection. State data associated with this Session MUST NOT be\nreused in any subsequent Session.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2.7]\n\nRetained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server,\nthey MUST NOT be deleted when the Session ends.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-8]\n\nIf the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request\nis accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated\nwith the Network Connection. The Will Message MUST be published when the\nNetwork Connection is subsequently closed unless the Will Message has\nbeen deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-9]\n\nIf the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the\nConnect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will\nMessage fields MUST be present in the payload.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-10]"

    "text": "Where the Topic Filter is not identical to any existing Subscription’s\nfilter, a new Subscription is created and all matching retained messages\nare sent.\n\nIf a Server receives a SUBSCRIBE packet that contains multiple Topic\nFilters it MUST handle that packet as if it had received a sequence of\nmultiple SUBSCRIBE packets, except that it combines their responses into\na single SUBACK response [MQTT-3.8.4-4] .\n\nThe SUBACK Packet sent by the Server to the Client MUST contain a return\ncode for each Topic Filter/QoS pair. This return code MUST either show\nthe maximum QoS that was granted for that Subscription or indicate that\nthe subscription failed [ MQTT-3 .8.4-5] . The Server might grant a\nlower maximum QoS than the subscriber requested. The QoS of Payload\nMessages sent in response to a Subscription MUST be the minimum of the\nQoS of the originally published message and the maximum QoS granted by\nthe Server. The server is permitted to send duplicate copies of a\nmessage to a subscriber in the case where the original message was\npublished with QoS 1 and the maximum QoS granted was QoS 0 [ MQTT-3\n.8.4-6] .\n\nNon normative examples If a subscribing Client has been granted maximum\nQoS 1 for a particular Topic Filter, then a QoS 0 Application Message\nmatching the filter is delivered to the Client at QoS 0. This means that\nat most one copy of the message is received by the Client. On the other\nhand a QoS 2 Message published to the same topic is downgraded by the\nServer to QoS 1 for delivery to the Client, so that Client might receive\nduplicate copies of the Message."

    "text": "If a Server deletes a Subscription It MUST complete the delivery of any\nQoS 1 or QoS 2 messages which it has started to send to the Client.\n\n[MQTT-3.10.4-4]\n\nThe Server MUST respond to an UNSUBSUBCRIBE request by sending an\nUNSUBACK packet. The UNSUBACK Packet MUST have the same Packet\nIdentifier as the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet.\n\n[MQTT-3.10.4-5]\n\nEven where no Topic Subscriptions are deleted, the Server MUST respond\nwith an UNSUBACK.\n\n[MQTT-3.10.4-6]\n\nIf a Server receives an UNSUBSCRIBE packet that contains multiple Topic\nFilters it MUST handle that packet as if it had received a sequence of\nmultiple UNSUBSCRIBE packets, except that it sends just one UNSUBACK\nresponse.\n\n[MQTT-3.12.4-1]\n\nThe Server MUST send a PINGRESP Packet in response to a PINGREQ packet.\n\n[MQTT-3.14.1-1]\n\nThe Server MUST validate that reserved bits are set to zero and\ndisconnect the Client if they are not zero.\n\n[MQTT-3.14.4-1]\n\nAfter sending a DISCONNECT Packet the Client MUST close the Network\nConnection.\n\n[MQTT-3.14.4-2]\n\nAfter sending a DISCONNECT Packet the Client MUST NOT send any more\nControl Packets on that Network Connection.\n\n[MQTT-3.14.4-3]\n\nOn receipt of DISCONNECT the Server MUST discard any Will Message\nassociated with the current connection without publishing it, as\ndescribed in Section 3.1.2.5 .\n\n[MQTT-4.1.0-1]\n\nThe Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration\nof the Session.\n\n[MQTT-4.1.0-2]\n\nA Session MUST last at least as long it has an active Network\nConnection.\n\n[MQTT-4.3.1-1]\n\nIn the QoS 0 delivery protocol, the Sender\n\n· MUST send a PUBLISH packet with QoS=0, DUP=0.\n\n[MQTT-4.3.2-1]\n\nIn the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender\n\n· MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new\nApplication Message to publish."

It MUST NOT be 3 (0x03).\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-15]\n\nIf the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will Retain Flag MUST be set to\n0.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-16]\n\nIf the Will Flag is set to 1 and If Will Retain is set to 0, the Server\nMUST publish the Will Message as a non-retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-17]\n\nIf the Will Flag is set to 1 and If Will Retain is set to 1, the Server\nMUST publish the Will Message as a retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-18]\n\nIf the User Name Flag is set to 0, a user name MUST NOT be present in\nthe payload.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-19]\n\nIf the User Name Flag is set to 1, a user name MUST be present in the\npayload.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-20]\n\nIf the Password Flag is set to 0, a password MUST NOT be present in the\npayload.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-21]\n\nIf the Password Flag is set to 1, a password MUST be present in the\npayload.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-22]\n\nIf the User Name Flag is set to 0, the Password Flag MUST be set to 0.\n\n[MQTT-3.1.2-23]"
